source: Rao and Ballard, Predictive coding in the visual cortex
external_claim: Higher-level units send predictions downward and feedforward signals carry residual errors; a trained hierarchical neural model reproduced selected receptive-field effects
fts_target: O_01; Res_n; projection/top-down and bottom-up loop
mapping: hierarchy + prediction/residual gives an explicit neural implementation of level-linked error refinement
limitation_or_defeat: visual-cortex model; does not define FTS levels, 0_A, Lift, or unique order

source: Andreas et al., Neural Module Networks
external_claim: Question structure can dynamically assemble reusable jointly trained neural modules into task-specific deep networks
fts_target: O_03; M/CH separation; compositional operator grammar
mapping: reusable modules + layout/assembly provide an implementation pattern for typed operations and compositional readings
limitation_or_defeat: network layout is learned task structure, not FTS ladder; no structured absence/provenance semantics

source: Graves et al., Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory
external_claim: A differentiable controller with read/write external memory learns structured graph and reasoning tasks and can generalize to new graphs
fts_target: O_03; W/0_W; recurrent closure; agentic memory layer
mapping: controller + explicit memory supplies a concrete substrate for persistence, retrieval and multi-step closure; graph tasks expose structured generalization
limitation_or_defeat: requires external memory and task-specific training; does not establish FTS-specific roles or a seven-level architecture
status_effect: result supports memory as an available design pattern, not FTS necessity

source: Le Morvan et al., NeuMiss networks
external_claim: Missingness indicators can be computationally necessary; a differentiable architecture using the indicator has risk and complexity results under stated missingness mechanisms
fts_target: 0_A; typed absence; O_03/O_14 as residual information
mapping: observed value and missingness state are distinct inputs; a typed mask can preserve information that imputation or omission loses
limitation_or_defeat: statistical missing data is not FTS structured absence; mechanisms and estimand differ; no claim about levels or semantics
status_effect: local bridge only; no status change

source: Che et al., Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values
external_claim: GRU-D incorporates missingness and elapsed time through trainable decay in recurrent updates for irregular multivariate time series
mapping: missingness and time-since-observation become typed update inputs instead of being silently discarded; supports structured handling of absence
limitation_or_defeat: healthcare time-series assumptions; decay is not FTS Tot/Lift; performance is task/domain-specific
status_effect: local bridge only; no status change

source: Ranzato and Tapparo, Generalized Strong Preservation by Abstract Interpretation
external_claim: For a fixed language, minimally refined abstract domains preserving concrete model checking can be characterized by completeness/greatest fixed points and refinement procedures
mapping: fixed-language preservation gives a typed template for refinement, projection and non-factorization tests
limitation_or_defeat: requires a formal language and semantic operators; not a theorem of FTS adjacency, cost, neural learning or global uniqueness
status_effect: local formal bridge; no status change

source: Cohen and Welling, Group Equivariant Convolutional Neural Networks
external_claim: Explicit group actions and weight sharing can reduce sample complexity and improve equivariant/invariant representation without increasing parameter count
mapping: provides an independent symmetry mechanism and a capacity-matched template for testing whether FTS phase/branch roles add value
limitation_or_defeat: known external formalism limits novelty of naming Z/2 or U(1); FTS must specify action and intertwining law

source: Dehaene et al., A neuronal model of a global workspace in effortful cognitive tasks
external_claim: Specialized processors and a recurrent globally connected workspace are proposed as a neural architecture with testable activation/connectivity predictions
fts_target: U7 window core; κ/agentic gate as diagnostic analogue; not U7 identity
mapping: specialized modules + recurrent broadcast is a possible external architecture for a closed/readable workspace
limitation_or_defeat: neurocognitive model, not an ANN proof; global workspace is not identical to Close(W,W) or κ

source: Lake et al., Building machines that learn and think like people
external_claim: Human-like learning systems are argued to require causal models, compositionality and learning-to-learn beyond pattern recognition
mapping: sets independent criteria by which an FTS skeleton would need to show composition, transfer and model-based generalization
limitation_or_defeat: argument is a programmatic review, not a test of FTS; does not validate any specific component

source: Kok and Lange, Predictive Processing: A Canonical Cortical Computation
external_claim: Predictive processing has support in hierarchical sensory organization but cortex as a whole is not simply one hierarchy and alternatives exist
mapping: limits any biological reading of a clean single ladder; supports testing local hierarchy rather than asserting whole-brain identity
limitation_or_defeat: secondary review; not direct FTS test; cortex-wide claim remains debated
status_effect: blocks T4 shortcut; no status change
